system.overview: The Metro SubwayLink is a heavy rail rapid transit line operated by the Maryland Transit Administration serving the Baltimore metropolitan area. Running 15.4 miles from Owings Mills in Baltimore County through downtown Baltimore to Johns Hopkins Hospital in East Baltimore, it is the only rapid transit line in Maryland. The system features both surface and deep-bore tunnel sections, with six underground stations in the downtown core.

history.title: Major Construction Begins
history.description: Full-scale construction begins on Section A, the initial 7.6-mile segment from Charles Center to Reisterstown Plaza.

history.title: System Opens
history.description: First 7.6-mile, 8-station segment from Charles Center to Reisterstown Plaza opens to passengers with 72 Budd UTV cars. Total construction cost was approximately $1.4 billion.

history.title: Owings Mills Extension Opens
history.description: 6.1-mile western extension from Reisterstown Plaza to Owings Mills opens with 3 new stations: Old Court, Milford Mill, and Owings Mills.

history.title: Johns Hopkins Extension Opens
history.description: Final 1.6-mile eastern extension opens with 2 new stations, Shot Tower and Johns Hopkins Hospital, completing the 14-station, 15.4-mile line.

history.title: Fleet Refurbishment Begins
history.description: All 100 Budd UTV cars undergo midlife refurbishment including seat reupholstery, floor replacement, and LED destination displays.

history.title: System Rebranded as SubwayLink
history.description: MTA Maryland rebrands all services under the unified 'Link' family. The Metro Subway becomes 'Metro SubwayLink' alongside CityLink buses and Light RailLink.

history.title: New Railcar Contract Awarded
history.description: MTA awards $400.5 million contract to Hitachi Rail for 78 new metro cars and Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC) signaling, the first fleet replacement in system history.

history.title: Hitachi Rail Cars Enter Service
history.description: New Hitachi Rail metro cars enter revenue service, marking the first fleet replacement in the system's 42-year history. The new cars feature AC propulsion, digital signage, and improved accessibility.

metro.name: Metro SubwayLink
metro.description: The Metro SubwayLink runs 15.4 miles from Owings Mills in western Baltimore County through downtown Baltimore to Johns Hopkins Hospital in East Baltimore. The line includes 6.2 miles of underground tunnel, 2.2 miles of elevated track, and 6.8 miles at grade. Trains operate every 8 minutes during rush hours and every 15 minutes during off-peak hours.

owings-mills.name: Owings Mills
owings-mills.description: Western terminus of the Metro SubwayLink. Surface station with approximately 3,500 parking spaces, the largest park-and-ride facility in the system.

old-court.name: Old Court
old-court.description: Surface station serving the Old Court Road area of Baltimore County. Opened as part of the 1987 Owings Mills extension.

milford-mill.name: Milford Mill
milford-mill.description: Surface station serving the Milford Mill area. The easternmost station added in the 1987 Owings Mills extension.

reisterstown-plaza.name: Reisterstown Plaza
reisterstown-plaza.description: Surface station adjacent to the Reisterstown Road Plaza shopping center. Original western terminus when the system opened in 1983.

rogers-avenue.name: Rogers Avenue
rogers-avenue.description: Surface station in the Park Heights neighborhood of northwest Baltimore.

west-cold-spring.name: West Cold Spring
west-cold-spring.description: Surface station near the intersection of Wabash Avenue and Cold Spring Lane in northwest Baltimore.

mondawmin.name: Mondawmin
mondawmin.description: Located near the Mondawmin Mall, this station marks the transition from surface running to the deep-bore tunnel section. Major bus transfer point.

penn-north.name: Penn North
penn-north.description: Deep underground station approximately 120 feet below street level, serving the Penn North neighborhood along Pennsylvania Avenue.

upton.name: Upton
upton.description: Underground station in the Upton neighborhood. Features Romare Bearden's jazz-themed mosaic artwork. Formerly known as Upton/Avenue Market.

state-center.name: State Center
state-center.description: Underground station near the Maryland State Center office complex. Walking distance to the Light RailLink Cultural Center stop for transfers.

lexington-market.name: Lexington Market
lexington-market.description: Underground station adjacent to the historic Lexington Market. Transfer point to the Light RailLink system via a short walk to the Lexington Market light rail stop on Howard Street.

charles-center.name: Charles Center
charles-center.description: Underground station in the heart of downtown Baltimore's Charles Center business district. Original eastern terminus when the system opened in 1983.

shot-tower.name: Shot Tower
shot-tower.description: Underground station near the historic Phoenix Shot Tower. Opened in 1995 as part of the Johns Hopkins extension. Formerly known as Shot Tower/Market Place.

johns-hopkins-hospital.name: Johns Hopkins Hospital
johns-hopkins-hospital.description: Eastern terminus of the Metro SubwayLink, serving the Johns Hopkins Hospital campus and East Baltimore. Opened in 1995, completing the 14-station line.

railcars.name: Budd UTV
railcars.description: The Budd Universal Transit Vehicles were the last railcars ever built by the Budd Company. Cars 100–171 were delivered in 1983 from a joint order shared with Miami Metrorail, and cars 172–199 arrived in 1986 for the Owings Mills extension. The fleet was refurbished in 2002–2005 and is currently being phased out in favor of new Hitachi Rail cars.

railcars.name: Hitachi Rail Metro
railcars.description: The Hitachi Rail metro cars are the first fleet replacement in system history, entering revenue service in January 2026. Built in Hagerstown, MD and Miami, FL as part of a $400.5 million contract that also includes Communications-Based Train Control signaling. The 78 cars operate as 39 married pairs and feature LED lighting, digital signage, and improved accessibility.
